findings.evidence: `rg` shows the definition at lines 85-91 is `∃ S : Finset ℂ, ... Tendsto ... (𝓝 v)`, while the single-point API has `theorem HasCauchyPVAt.unique` in `CauchyPrincipalValue.lean:159`; no analogous `HasCauchyPV.unique` or finset-independence lemma appears in the new file.
findings.fix: Add the missing characteristic API, at least `HasCauchyPV.unique` (or the enlargement/inertness lemma needed to prove it), and the corresponding existence-to-canonical-value interface; otherwise expose a prescribed-set predicate first and reserve the S-free value predicate until independence of `S` is available.
findings.issue: `HasCauchyPV γ a b f v` existentially hides the excision finset `S`, but the public API provides no uniqueness or finset-independence theorem for the value `v`. This leaves an existence-and-value predicate whose value cannot be shown functional when two witnesses use different `S`.

summary: The new S-free value predicate exposes an existential choice of excision set without the characteristic API that makes the value well-defined, so downstream users cannot reason that a principal value is unique.
